title: A Radical Reframe
use_cases: Use when developing a narrative framework that aligns character motivation with plot progression
Implement when troubleshooting a story where plot points feel forced or inorganic
Configure when designing character arcs that dictate structural changes in a manuscript
Use when mapping the causal relationship between a character's internal fear and their external actions
content: There are no plot-driven stories. There are no character-driven stories. There are only character-driven plots. Story emerges from people in action—what they want, what they fear, what they do under pressure. Plot is the trail left behind by a character pursuing something, failing, recalibrating, and pursuing again. When a character changes direction, the plot does too. The best plots are not designed—they are inevitable, because the characters can’t do otherwise.
